messages:
maria: quick design review please — i'm about to merge a PR for the routing policies editor. main changes: drag-to-reorder rule list, inline conflict validation, and a preview/simulation panel. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/PRIVATE-ROUTING-EDITOR. can folks scan for UX gotchas (keyboard nav, copy, accessibility) before i merge into beta?

devin: skimming — nice. couple quick nits: the drag handle needs a stronger affordance (thin dots are easy to miss). suggest: full-width handle region + visible priority badge on the left. when dragging show a ghost placeholder and a clear insertion line.

alex: validation copy: current text says "Rule conflicts with higher priority rule" — too terse and a bit scary. propose: "This rule never runs because a higher-priority rule matches the same requests. Consider changing the order or refining conditions." keep it 1–2 sentences and add a "Learn more" link to docs.

sam: preview panel is great — two suggestions: 1) show the sample request (method/path/headers) used for the preview and highlight which condition matched, 2) add a toggle for "simulate with KV cache on/off" because routing decisions differ with cached prefixes. also, don't block saving if preview fails; surface a non-blocking warning instead.

maria: thanks. on the priority badge vs implicit order question — product leaning toward an explicit numeric priority field (so analytics and logs show stable ids). reordering mutates those numbers. any objections?

devin: ok with explicit numbers as long as drag + keyboard reorder updates them live. keyboard: support focus on the rule row, then allow Alt+Up / Alt+Down (or Ctrl) to move. ensure aria-grabbed and aria-dropeffect roles for screen readers.

alex: +1 for numbers. additional validation UX: don't dump every conflict inline by default. collapse conflicts under a single badge on the rule row, with "show details" to expand the list. and add an "auto-resolve" suggestion that proposes a reorder to avoid conflicts (user must confirm).

sam: accessibility nits: color contrast for the error state is low on the current mock (red #e06 vs bg). bump to WCAG AA contrast, and add an icon so color isn't the only signal. preview panel should have a skip link and not trap focus permanently; when it opens, focus should move to the panel heading, and Esc should close.

maria: good points. technical question for infra teams: when we auto-resolve or programmatically reassign priorities, we should keep the numeric gap small (like step=10) to allow future inserts. devin, can you show numbers with 10-step spacing in figma?

devin: yeah i'll update the frame — using 10 increments (100, 90, 80) visually and the UI will recompute on reorder. also adding a subtle drag ghost and stronger touch target for the handle.

alex: copy follow-up: for the inline validation details include one-line remediation + CTA to docs. example: "Remediation: Move this rule below rule 14 or narrow the path condition. Learn more." keep the tone prescriptive but helpful.

sam: preview simulation UX: show a small timeline: request -> evaluate conditions -> matched rule -> action. example snippet in preview: ```{\n  "input":"GET /api/users?page=1",\n  "matched_rule":"rule-17",\n  "reason":"first-match: path prefix /api/users"\n}``` this helps debug why a rule didn't run.

maria: we also discussed whether reordering should be optimistic (UI-only until save) or immediate (sync to backend on-drop). leaning optimistic to let users make multiple moves then commit. infra: is that okay?

devin: optimistic is better for UX. just show a dirty state on the save button and a small toast on successful apply. but the numeric badge should reflect the tentative order so previews match what the user sees.

alex: minor: change validation label color from pure red to an orange/warning when it's a "possible" conflict vs a hard "never runs" conflict. reduces alarmism.

sam: accessibility checklist for final PR: keyboard reorder, aria-live for preview results, descriptive aria-labels for badges, color+icon for statuses, focus management on preview open/close. i'll put a short test plan in the PR.

maria: action items: devin update figma (handle, numeric badges, insertion ghost), alex rewrite validation copy + add docs link and auto-resolve text, sam prototype keyboard reorder + focus behavior + test plan. i'll adjust product notes and aim to land into beta next week.

simulate-bot: quick simulation run on staging preview endpoint -> 200 OK. sample match returned: ```{\n  "input":"GET /api/users?page=1",\n  "matched_rule":"rule-17",\n  "reason":"first-match by path prefix",\n  "preview_kv_cache":false\n}```

devin: :thumbsup:

alex: +1

sam: thanks — i'll start the keyboard prototype today.

maria: thanks all — i'll update the PR description with these notes and tag reviewers. merging to beta after figma/PR updates.
